review.itemreviewed: Nano Puff Insulated Jacket - Men's
review.reviewBody: This is my favorite jacket of all time. Works when it's hot, works when it's cold. Last forever. Patagonia's lifetime warranty is amazing and easy. They have replaced old jackets before. This requires pretty much no maintenance and easily adapts to every environment (e.g. putting it on and taking it off helps a lot with temperature). Super light and small too.
review.name: Wonderful jacket

review.itemreviewed: Nano Puff Insulated Jacket - Men's
review.reviewBody: Packed these for the summer in the Alps and already found them helpful in Normandy. Light weight, warm for moderate cold, looks good, form fitting. Overall the perfect lightweight jacket for moderate cold. At 12c with a driving wind and high humidity t was pleasant driving away the damp cold. Will get to the Alps next week but anticipate it preforming well there.
review.name: Great lightweight packable Jacket

review.itemreviewed: Nano Puff Insulated Jacket - Men's
review.reviewBody: Bought this as a "tweener" 40's jacket when my Arc'teryx Atom AR is too warm. So far could not be happier. Super light puffer that can also be used under a shell for certain activities. Not the cheapest option but at 20% off and given how long a good jacket can last, something I won't even think about. Terrific product.
review.name: Great jacket for many years ahead

review.itemreviewed: Torrentshell 3L Jacket - Men's
review.reviewBody:
I bought this coat for a 10-day trip to the Azores. It rained nearly every day, and didn't stop me for a second! The Torrentshell kept me dry and comfortable, even on a 7 hour climb of Mt. Pico with rain blowing from all directions.

- I love the blue color, it looks great.
- the jacket, like all raincoats can be a little warm in warm weather. It is an effective windbreaker and the pit zips help- I was pretty comfortable wearing it with a T-shirt underneath in 65 degree weather.
- initially the jacket is a bit stiff and crinkly from the factory, but after a few uses and packing/unpacking it loosens up nicely.
- zippers and pulls are great quality.
-lightweight and packable in a pocket.
-I am 6'1", 190lbs and the Large leaves plenty of room for layering without looking baggy.

I LOVED having this jacket and highly recommend it.
review.name: Love it!

review.itemreviewed: Torrentshell 3L Jacket - Men's
review.reviewBody: Excellent product: sturdy, well-made, effective, smooth-operating protected zippers, large zipped armpit openings, ample Velcro to secure jacket around wrists, ample hood.  My only complaints are that there aren’t any inner pockets, and the durable, high-quality material is on the ‘crunchy’ side, so to speak, and is therefore fairly noisy when putting on, taking off, and moving around.
review.name: Excellent rain-protection and quality

review.itemreviewed: Torrentshell 3L Jacket - Men's
review.reviewBody:
I just spent 14 days in Alaska and it rained pretty much every day. This jacket definitely kept me dry and it kept the wind out but you’ll want to layer because it won’t really keep you warm. 

The only negative is that it sounds like you’re wearing a Doritos bag. It’s really noisy. Other than that, it’s great!
review.name: Nice raincoat

review.itemreviewed: Down Sweater Hooded Jacket - Men's
review.reviewBody:
My lifestyle is more Urban Explorer than hard-core hiker, but I have spent my fair share of days traipsing about Bavaria & the Scottish Highlands.  I have generally had good luck with Patagonia and have always liked their products with just a couple of exceptions.  

The Good & the Not So Good- I have a Down Sweater Vest that is incredible.  It warm, the fit is great and it has held up well over the past 2-3 years of regular use.  I've found it to be quite versatile worn over a lighter mid-layer or when used as a mid layer under a shell/jacket for extra warmth.   I've also owned two Patagonia Nanopuff Jackets, both treated virtually equally.  One has been brilliant, the other began losing the threading between the baffles within 6 months.

I recently ordered a new Patagonia Down Sweater Jacket and as soon as it was removed from packaging, noticed it was shedding down in several places- Not large bits, just a number of small puffs.  This concerned me enough that I returned it and purchased a RAB Down Jacket instead, another brand I've had great luck with.

Perhaps the Down Sweater jacket I received was just a one-ff, but I have noticed other reviews mentioning the same issue.  I will still consider Patagonia gear in the future, but I'll likely stick with RAB for any down products.  I'll leave a review of that coat once I've used it for a bit.
review.name: WANTED TO LOVE IT, BUT...

review.itemreviewed: Down Sweater Hooded Jacket - Men's
review.reviewBody: Very warm. I buy a size bigger to wear a hoodie under and I’m always comfortable during New England winters. My beef is like most gear I’ve owned back in my the day, the quality of the new stuff seems to have gone by the wayside. I own a few Patagonia jackets and my older ones are still looking good. New ones are 100$ more in just the last couple years. I feel the new jackets tear easily. Caught a thorn on the arm and it shredded the jacket, my old jacket doesn’t have a tear on it after years of wear. The issue I notice the most is the feathers seem to come out of ever seam they can fin. The jacket I recently got has feathers coming out all over it. My old Patagonia, not a feather to been lost, sigh, I know I sound like an old man yelling at clouds but they just don’t make them like they used to. Still a nice warm jacket with a pretty ethical company so you make the call
review.name: Patagonia down hoodie

review.itemreviewed: Down Sweater Hooded Jacket - Men's
review.reviewBody: I ordered size Medium, as I wear in my other Patagonia fleeces and jackets. The body and arms fit well as expected. The jacket is warm, soft, and light, and a joy to wear. However, the hood when fully zipped is so tight that it digs into my chin and restricts my head movement. In other words, with the zipper in the fully up position the bottom of the face opening is on my chin and tight against it. Even if I pull it down below my chin it's still tight, digging in beneath my mouth. There is a cinch cord in the back. It comes fully extended when new, but just to make sure I wasn't mis-using it I cinched it tight. Yep, it was even tighter. This is really a mystery to me how the hood was designed. Unfortunately I had to return this jacket because I would never be able to use the hood fully zipped and then - what is the point of having a hooded jacket.
review.name: Nice Jacket But Hood Too Tight to Use

review.itemreviewed: Fitz Roy Down Hooded Jacket - Men's
review.reviewBody:
I purchased the Fitz Roy jacket in hopes that it would meet my needs for shoulder-season river trips where the night temps can drop into the 20's-30's. The jacket fit well with a fuller cut to allow for layering and the sleeve and body length were perfect. The down fill is a step up from their Down Sweater Hoody which I own, but still lighter than my Rab Neutrino, which I was hoping to replace. But with layering it would have met my needs.

The issue I found was with the design of the hood and the single-pull drawcord for adjustment. Fully zipped up, the collar came to the bottom of my chin. With the hood on there was a lot of open space around my face and neck because the opening is so large. Using the single-pull drawcord, I can get the hood snug around my face and chin but then the tension of the drawcord circling around the top of my head is uncomfortably tight. This isn't the case with my Down Sweater Hoody where the hood fits snugly over my chin and around my face when zipped up with only a small amount of tension on the drawcord. 

If there wasn't an issue with the hood design I would give this a 5-star rating. I expect more from Patagonia when designing functional outdoor gear.
review.name: Poor hood design
comment: The Fitz Roy has a hood designed to fit a helmet. So, it doesn't really deserve a lower rating for doing what it's suppose to do.

review.itemreviewed: Fitz Roy Down Hooded Jacket - Men's
review.reviewBody:
I was looking for a jacket to fill the gap between the down sweater hoody and a full-on stand alone down parka.   Upon inspection I can see this jacket will fill this spot perfectly - its just heavy enough to add real insulation under a shell or even be stand-alone with a decent layer below. 

Really like the chest pockets as they are well designed for a phone or GPS. 

I am 6'3 and 175 and I like the XL as it has plenty of room below should I layer and the arms are plenty long.
review.name: Perfect Midweight Puff

review.itemreviewed: Fitz Roy Down Hooded Jacket - Men's
review.reviewBody: Not up to the usual Patagonia quality.  800 down fill not what it used to be.
review.name: Not warm and doesn't fit right

Assign a score between 0 and 100 to the following item
        based on how relevant it is to the user's question. Use your knowledge from other sources, about the item, to make a judgement. 
        If the score is above 50, provide a short description of the item highlighting the relevance to the user's question, without mentioning the user's question.
        
        In the description, do NOT 
        - mention the user's question
        - refer to the site
        - mention the score
        - mention the type of the item 

        If the score is below 75, in the description, include the reason why it is still relevant.
        The description you generate should be in English.
          

        The user's question is: \"{request.query}\". The item's description in schema.org format is \"{item.description}\".
